data.title: Paramount Skydance to Transfer Stock to NY Stock Exchange
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Paramount Skydance is transferring its stock listing from Nasdaq to the New York Stock Exchange.

The company said Friday that its board voluntarily withdrew the listing of Class B shares from Nasdaq to transfer them to NYSE.

Shares are expected to stop listing on Nasdaq on Oct. 5, and start trading on NYSE on Oct. 6.

The listing change comes as Paramount is set to close its mega-merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.

data.title: Eli Lilly Gets Expanded Label Approval From FDA for Alopecia Drug
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Eli Lilly received expanded label approval from the Food and Drug Administration for Olumiant, a drug for pediatric patients 12 years of age or older with severe alopecia areata.

The company said Friday that the FDA had approved the expanded U.S. label for the drug, known generically as baricitinib, based on the results of a Phase 3 study. Olumiant was previously approved for adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis and severe alopecia areata.

"The visible and often extensive hair loss that comes with severe alopecia areata can have a profound impact on anyone, especially adolescents who are at a pivotal stage of life," Lilly Immunology president Adrienne Brown said. "Expanding Olumiant to patients as young as 12 provides them a much-needed treatment choice and reinforces our commitment to advancing care for people living with immune-mediated diseases."

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Merck, Daiichi Sankyo Withdraw Application for Accelerated Approval of Lung Cancer Treatment
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Merck & Co. and Daiichi Sankyo have withdrawn their application seeking accelerated approval for a small cell lung cancer treatment, saying the data they had submitted to the Food and Drug Administration was insufficient.

The two companies said they decided to withdraw the Biologics License Application for ifinatamab deruxtecan after discussions with the FDA that the data included in the application, including the results of a Phase 2 trial, do not meet the requirements for an accelerated approval.

The companies continue to enroll patients in a Phase 3 trial of the drug. Two other Phase 3 trials evaluating the drug as a treatment for prostate cancer and a form of carcinoma are also under way.

"While we are disappointed that the current dataset are not supportive of an approval at this time, we are continuing to evaluate the role of ifinatamab deruxtecan in patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer and other types of difficult-to-treat cancer," said Marjorie Green, Merck Research Laboratories head of oncology.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Nuclear firm Holtec withdraws US IPO filing after suspending offering
data.description:
Holtec Nuclear withdrew its initial public offering registration statement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday, more than a week after it suspended its planned IPO.

Here are some key details:

  • The Camden, New Jersey-based nuclear technology ​company, which was expected to go public last week, initially postponed the offering, citing adverse sentiment impacting the equity markets and the nuclear sector.

  • "We attribute the ongoing retreat of the nuclear energy sector to a perfect storm of adverse developments, driven primarily by uncertainty over data center development, which has compounded a set of pre-existing headwinds," Holtec said in its statement last week.

  • At the time, Holtec said it planned to maintain its registration statement on file with the US SEC.

  • However, in a filing on Friday, it said it was "seeking withdrawal of the registration statement because it no longer wishes to conduct a public offering of securities at this time."

data.title: TSX ends near flat for the week as financial shares rally
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

Canada's main stock index ended higher on Friday, led by gains for financial shares, as domestic bond yields pulled back from multi-year highs.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index ended up 94.43 points, or 0.3%, at 35,800.89, a day after posting its lowest closing level in eight days. For the week, the index was barely changed, dipping 0.02%.

  • "Rising bond yields are a headwind for the market because it suggests there's expectations of higher interest rates and rate hikes," said Colin Cieszynski, chief market strategist at SIA Wealth Management.

  • "So the decline in bond yields is short-term, at least, positive," Cieszynski said. "The headwinds fade a little bit and that's helped the markets pick up today."

  • The Canadian 10-year yield (CA10YT=RR) eased 7.5 basis points to 3.923%, after touching its highest level since October 2023 at 4.011% during Thursday's session.

  • Preliminary domestic data showed that wholesale trade declined 1.5% in August from July.

  • Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) added 1.1%, helped by gains for major banks.

  • National Bank of Canada announced plans to buy back up to 10 million shares. Its shares ended 1.4% higher.

  • Shares of auto parts supplier Magna International rose 4.7%, which helped lift consumer discretionary (.GSPTTCD) by 2.2%.

  • Energy was a drag, falling 0.8%, as U.S. crude oil futures settled 2.3% lower at $92.41 a barrel on mounting hopes for a truce between the US and Iran.

  • Technology was down 1.1%, with BlackBerry shares falling 5.7%.

data.title: H&R REIT ANNOUNCES RECORD DATE AND MEETING DATE FOR SPECIAL MEETING IN CONNECTION WITH PROPOSED TRANSACTION
data.description:
TORONTO, Sept. 25, 2026 /CNW/ -- H&R Real Estate Investment Trust ("H&R" or the "REIT") (TSX: HR.UN) announced today that it has filed the notice of meeting and record date in respect of its special meeting (the "Special Meeting") of holders of trust units of H&R, special voting units of H&R and units of H&R Portfolio Limited Partnership designated as "Class B Limited Participation LP Units" (collectively, the "H&R REIT Voting Securityholders") fixing the record date and meeting date in respect of the Special Meeting. The record date for the determination of those H&R REIT Voting Securityholders entitled to receive notice of and vote at the Special Meeting has been fixed as October 2, 2026, and the Special Meeting will be held on November 13, 2026 in a virtual-only format by way of live audio webcast, consistent with the REIT's customary practice. Materials in connection with the Special Meeting are expected to be filed on SEDAR+ and posted on H&R's website on or about October 8, 2026, and sent to H&R REIT Voting Securityholders shortly thereafter.

The purpose of the Special Meeting is for H&R REIT Voting Securityholders to consider H&R's previously announced transaction pursuant to which GO Residential Real Estate Investment Trust ("GO REIT") and 1001700058 Ontario Inc., on behalf of a consortium of co-purchasers (which includes a fund affiliated with Blackstone Real Estate, a partnership managed by Crestpoint Real Estate Investments Ltd. and a company controlled by members of the family of Tom Hofstedter, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of H&R), have agreed to acquire all of the assets of H&R by way of a court-approved plan of arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) pursuant to which holders of trust units of the REIT will receive a mix of cash and GO REIT units (the "Transaction").

For further details relating to the Transaction, please refer to H&R's material change report in respect of the Transaction filed under H&R's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca. data.title: Walmart Says It Won't Use Dynamic Pricing — WSJ
data.description:
By Sarah Nassauer

Walmart, weighing in on the controversial practice of dynamic pricing, says consumers have nothing to fear from its future tactics.

On Friday Walmart Chief Executive John Furner posted a statement online that said the retailer is not using personal information like income, shopping history or level of need to set prices and won't do so in the future.

"We don't set different prices based on who you are or the time of day, and we won't," said Furner. It would violate Walmart's promise to provide everyday low prices, he added.

Consumers are worried about how retailers could use new technologies to set or quickly change prices to extract the largest profit from each purchase.

Walmart drew some of the ire earlier this year, after introducing electronic shelf price tags in its stores. Fair-pricing advocates and people on social media expressed concern the retailer could use the tags to price items based on need or other factors.

Walmart executives have said repeatedly they only change electronic prices overnight when stores are closed and use the tools to reduce the labor costs associated with changing paper price tags.

Furner's post might not be enough to quiet the critics. Lindsay Owens, chief executive of economic-policy advocacy group Groundwork Collaborative, urged Walmart to pull the electronic shelf price tags as well as patents that describe technology that could enable dynamic pricing based on need or past behavior.

Walmart didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on its pricing patents.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Physical crude grades mixed amid end-of-month trading
data.description:
By Liz Hampton

US cash crude grades were mixed on Friday in thin trading, brokers said, with some participants out of the market to attend industry events.

Oil futures fell roughly 2% to close out the week amid hopes of a truce between the US and Iran, and amid talk of a possible ban on US diesel exports, which could hurt crude demand. US West Texas Intermediate futures were down about 8% for the week.

Meanwhile, oil flows out of the Strait of Hormuz reached 33.7 million barrels in the week starting September 20, according to preliminary data from ship tracker Kpler, in line with previous weeks.

US oilfield service firms added rigs for the third week in a row, energy services company Baker Hughes said on Friday. Oil rigs rose by three to 455, the highest since mid-August.

  • Light Louisiana Sweet (WTC-LLS) for October delivery was last at a $2.50 premium to West Teas Intermediate crude futures ​, but that market had little activity on Friday, dealers said

  • Mars Sour (WTC-MRS) traded at a $5 discount to US crude futures, up $2.50 from the prior day

  • WTI Midland (WTC-WTM) fell sharply, trading at a $2.5 discount to US crude futures

  • West Texas Sour (WTC-WTS) traded at a $3 discount to crude futures ​, down $1 a barrel from the prior day

  • WTI at East Houston (WTC-MEH), also known as MEH, at a 75 cent premium to US West Texas Intermediate futures, versus a $2 premium the previous day

  • ICE Brent November futures fell $2.28 to settle at $104.32 a barrel on Friday​.

  • WTI November crude futures fell $2.2 to settle at $92.41 a barrel on Friday​.
